doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Learning the trumpet with Doc Cheatham's help
summary: Carter practiced on his own with Cheatham as the only teacher and bought a Conn 22B on his advice.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: While we’re talking about your multi-instrumental activities, we talked about the trumpet and how you began playing the trumpet. I just wanted to pick up on that for a second. According to what we discussed the other day, you really had been playing the trumpet virtually a matter of months before you already recorded on it and recorded a masterpiece such as Once Upon a Time and had already actually recorded one brief solo on the first Benny Carter Orchestra session of March ’33.
I think it was on Synthetic Love, kind of a melody statement.
Oh, did I play a trumpet on that?
Yeah, briefly. I think that’s the first instance.
But this is really from the end of ’32 when Doc Cheatham began passing you the trumpet.
Yeah, you can blame it all on Doc Cheatham. It’s all his fault.
[laughs] But did you do any intensive practicing, away from Doc Cheatham, obviously?

Oh, I must have. Of course. Yes, of course. You don’t pick up a trumpet and just, you know, cold turkey or cold chops. So I’m sure I spent some time woodshedding at home or something, you know. Yeah, sure.
Did you ever go to any other teachers, as you did with the saxophone . . .
. . . other than working with Doc Cheatham?
No, the only teacher was Doc Cheatham.
How about method books or something? You mentioned a few for a sax that you might have consulted, but . . .

Method books, I don’t know that I had even a trumpet method book at that time, but later I did come across and get the . . . what is it? Can’t even remember the name of it now. Could have been Hubert Clark [phonetic] or someone other. I don’t remember. Arbor [phonetic] or something. I can’t remember the name of the book now, but I think it’s a book that was kind of like the bible for trumpet players. Arbin [phonetic], I think it was.
Do you remember buying your first instrument, your first trumpet, other than the one when you were a kid and worked in the laundry?
Well, I don’t really remember, but it was recommended by Doc, and I know that it was a Conn 22B. That’s about all I remember.
